description:
Redwood Inference is scaling a PLG-led motion (self-serve Hosted API adoption) into a consistent, measurable sales-assisted expansion motion for Dedicated and Private deployments. This project implements product-usage thresholds and intent signals (e.g., sustained spend, concurrency, error-rate pain, security feature interest, region/residency needs, repeated pricing-page visits, “contact sales” events) and routes them into HubSpot with clear ownership rules, deduplication, and a follow-up cadence/playbook.

Goals:
- Define a small, high-signal set of “sales-worthy” triggers with low false positives.
- Build a reliable signal pipeline (aggregation, scoring, enrichment) and route outputs into HubSpot (company timeline events, tasks, sequences) and optionally Slack notifications.
- Operationalize a follow-up playbook (persona-based messaging, cadence, handoff to SE/CS, suppression/opt-out rules) and ensure compliance with privacy/security expectations.
- Measure impact end-to-end: signal → outreach → meetings → pipeline → conversion; iterate thresholds and messaging.

Scope:
- Data/Signals: usage aggregation windows (7/14/30d), spend/token thresholds by tier, burst/concurrency thresholds, repeated rate-limit hits, repeated model-routing failures, interest in Dedicated/Private (docs/console clicks), “security questionnaire” intent, region/residency constraints.
- Routing: ownership logic (geo/segment), dedupe windows, cool-down periods, enrichment (company domain, industry, team size band where available), and suppression rules (active opportunities, existing CSM-managed enterprise accounts, explicit opt-out).
- Activation: HubSpot workflows to create tasks + enroll sequences; Slack notifications to #sales (and #customer-success for expansion candidates); lightweight internal dashboards.
- Governance: data retention/access control for signals, auditability, and documentation for Sales/CS.

Stakeholders:
- Product: Nikhil Sharma (Hosted API), Marissa Cole / Paula Mendes (Console & telemetry requirements), Chris Osei (Product Ops).
- Engineering: Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman (Telemetry), Cole Summers (Quotas & billing hooks), platform/integrations engineers.
- GTM: Jordan Blake (CRO), Stephanie Nguyen / Lukas Meyer (Sales leadership), Grace O’Connor (SDR), Ben Carter (Growth Marketing), Markus Klein (Solutions Engineering).
- Customer Success/Support: Jasmine Liu, Rachel Kim, Dev Patel.
- Security/Legal/IT: Dr. Aisha Rahman / Marcus Lin (security), Michael Grant (legal), David Kim (Biz Systems/HubSpot admin).

Timeline (phased, ~8–10 weeks):
1) Discovery + definitions (2 weeks): finalize signals/thresholds, routing rules, playbook draft, pilot cohort.
2) Build + integrate (4–5 weeks): aggregation jobs, scoring, HubSpot write path, workflow setup, Slack notifications, monitoring.
3) Pilot + iteration (2–3 weeks): run with limited cohort, tune thresholds and messaging, fix data quality/dedupe.
4) Rollout + KPI reporting (ongoing): expand to all self-serve accounts, weekly review of conversion metrics and false positives.

Key deliverables:
- PRD + technical design for signals and routing.
- HubSpot workflow configuration + ownership mapping.
- Sales/SDR cadence playbook and templates.
- Runbooks/monitoring for the signal pipeline and HubSpot sync.
- KPI dashboard spec and early results readout.

Constraints/risks:
- False positives can damage trust; must include dedupe + cool-down + suppression.
- Privacy/compliance: limit PII, document data usage, restrict visibility for sensitive accounts.
- Data latency and reliability: signals must arrive quickly enough for timely outreach, with alerting for pipeline failures.

files.description: PRD: problem statement, goals/non-goals, signal taxonomy, tier-specific thresholds, routing requirements, success metrics, pilot plan, and rollout stages.
Technical design spec: event sources, aggregation windows, scoring logic, dedupe/cool-down rules, HubSpot API objects to write (company events/tasks), and failure handling.
Sales/SDR enablement playbook: trigger-specific talk tracks, objection handling, persona templates (eng lead, platform, security), and the 1/3/7/14-day cadence.
Guidance mapping signals to recommended offers (Hosted→Dedicated, Dedicated→Private), when to propose commits/discounts, and guardrails for free-credit exceptions.
Data governance doc (restricted): what signal data is stored, retention, access control, auditability, acceptable use for outreach, and opt-out handling.
Runbook: monitoring, alerting, common failure modes (HubSpot rate limits, retries, duplicates), backfills, and how to verify a signal end-to-end.
Working spreadsheet (sheet): historical self-serve cohorts, candidate thresholds, estimated lead volumes, false-positive sampling notes, and segment breakdowns.
Sheet: pilot cohort accounts, domains, region/segment, assigned AE/SDR/SE, suppression flags, and notes from CS.
Doc: draft email/LinkedIn sequences for each signal type (rate-limit pain, spend growth, security intent), with A/B variants and personalization tokens.
Doc: KPI definitions (signal→task→meeting→SQL→pipeline), attribution rules, dashboards needed, and data quality checks.
Slides: early pilot results, example wins/losses, false positives, changes to thresholds, and next rollout decision ask.
